title: Formalized completeness and arithmetic provability

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Derive formalized existential completeness and the three derivability conditions for the specified PA predicate.
abstract: An existential arithmetic statement with a bounded matrix says that a finite calculation has suitable witnesses. The bounded proof builders let PA turn those same witnesses into a code for a proof of the statement. This gives formalized completeness: PA proves that each such statement implies its own provability, with parameters handled by an explicit numeral-substitution operation. We use that result and the checked operation combining proofs to establish the three derivability conditions for the fixed proof predicate. Its consistency sentence is then tied to the same checker throughout; replacing it by another formula requires an internal comparison, beyond agreement in the natural numbers.
